products.name: Sketch AI
products.note: Design tool AI; macOS native; local processing option; EU design data

reading.body:
Sketch is a design tool with AI capabilities that offers local processing as an option, distinguishing it from cloud-dependent alternatives in a market where data residency and privacy have become competitive factors.

The presence of a local processing option matters because AI inference at the edge, rather than in remote data centers, reduces dependence on the grid and compute infrastructure that constrain AI scaling elsewhere. For a design tool, this trades real-time collaborative speed for user control over where their work is processed. The company's emphasis on EU data handling and independence from larger platforms suggests a deliberate positioning against the centralized compute model.

This data does not cover Sketch's actual architecture, whether local processing is the default or optional, the computational load it handles on-device versus in the cloud, or how many users opt for it. It also does not address the power or cooling implications of pushing processing to individual machines rather than shared data centers. For understanding AI's relationship to the grid, the distinction between where inference happens is crucial, but the data only flags that Sketch offers the choice.

profile_text.body:
Sketch is a for-profit design software company founded in 2010 and headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands. Its flagship product is a macOS-native design editor that the company describes as built around a focused interface, an infinite canvas, and zero distractions, intended specifically for designers rather than project managers, developers, or clients. The tool covers design, prototyping, collaboration, and developer handoff within a single environment.

Sketch offers an AI-capable tier tracked under the name Sketch AI, categorized as an image and graphic design tool. According to the held facts, it includes a local processing option and handles EU design data, which aligns with the company's stated emphasis on privacy and independence from larger platform ecosystems. The company describes itself as independent and notes it makes its own decisions on matters ranging from privacy to pricing.

No litigation, MCP server registrations, SEC filings, or patent records are present in the available data.
